title: CBS, OBS and the responsibility assignment matrix
blurb: Outline how a project manager uses a CBS, an OBS and a RACI-style RAM to budget, assign ownership and control the work.
question: On an office relocation, the IT hardware budget has overrun and two team leads each thought the other was handling the network cabling. Which three structures would have shown where the money was going, who is involved, and who owns each piece of work?

teach.h: Three more structures, three more questions
teach.body: Once the work breakdown structure (WBS) shows the work, the project manager still needs to know how much each part will cost and who will do it. The cost breakdown structure (CBS) answers HOW MUCH. The organisational breakdown structure (OBS) answers WHO is involved. The responsibility assignment matrix (RAM) brings the work and the people together to show WHO DOES WHAT. Our example: Calder & Moss Ltd moving its head office.

A CBS breaks the project's costs down into cost categories or accounts aligned to the WBS. Each work package's estimated cost rolls up into the budget, so the project manager can allocate budget to each part of the work and later track actual spend against it. When costs overrun, the CBS shows exactly where. In short: budgeting and cost control.

teach.caption: The top level mirrors the WBS, so every cost belongs to a piece of work. An IT hardware overrun shows up in account 2, not hidden in a single total.

teach.body: An OBS is the hierarchy of the organisations, teams and people involved in the project, showing reporting lines and lines of authority: the WHO. It can include external suppliers and contractors as well as internal teams. The project manager uses it to see who is available to own work, who reports to whom, and where to escalate.

teach.h: OBS: who is involved in the move
teach.caption: People and teams, not tasks. External suppliers appear under the person who manages them.

teach.body: A RAM is a matrix formed by combining the WBS with the OBS: work packages down one side, people or teams across the top. Each cell shows that person's role in that piece of work. It is often drawn in RACI form. Its job is to make sure every work package has a clear owner, with no gaps and no duplication.

letters.sub: Ultimately answerable; signs it off. Only one per package
Gives input before or during the work (two-way)
Kept up to date on progress (one-way)

teach.h: RAM in RACI form: the office move
head: Work package
PM
Facilities
IT lead
teach.caption: WBS down the side, OBS across the top. Cabling now has one Responsible person (the IT lead), so nobody can assume someone else is doing it.

teach.h: How the project manager uses them
items: CBS: allocate the budget to each work package and track actual costs against it.
OBS: understand who is involved, reporting lines and who can own work.
RAM: assign ownership so every work package has an owner, and clarify roles.
All three: support communication (who to consult and inform) and control (who answers for cost and delivery).

teach.text: Don't mix up the letters: the OBS shows PEOPLE, the CBS shows COSTS, the WBS shows WORK. A RAM is the WBS × OBS matrix; RACI is just a popular format for a RAM. And Responsible (does the work) is not the same as Accountable (answers for it and signs it off).

items: CBS: project costs broken into cost categories or accounts aligned to the WBS: budgeting and cost control.
OBS: the hierarchy of organisations, teams and people involved: the WHO, with reporting lines.
RAM = WBS × OBS: shows who is responsible for each work package, often as RACI.
RACI: Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed; one Accountable per work package.
The PM uses them to allocate budget, assign ownership, clarify roles and support communication and control.

summary: You can now outline how a project manager uses a CBS to allocate and control budget, an OBS to show who is involved and how they report, and a RAM (WBS × OBS, often in RACI form) to give every work package a clear owner. You can also tell the four RACI roles apart.

A.q: Complete the statement: a responsibility assignment matrix is created by mapping the ______ against the ______.
A.why: A RAM combines the work breakdown structure (the work) with the organisational breakdown structure (the people).

whyNot.0: The PBS and CBS show products and costs; neither shows who does the work.
whyNot.1: The OBS shows people, but the CBS shows costs, not the work to be assigned.
whyNot.3: The PBS shows products and a risk breakdown structure shows risk sources; neither pairing assigns work.

A.q: In a RACI chart, who is ultimately answerable for a work package and signs it off?
A.why: The Accountable person is ultimately answerable for the work package and signs it off. There should be only one per package.

whyNot.0: Responsible people do the work, but are not necessarily the ones who answer for it.
whyNot.1: Consulted people give their input before or during the work.
whyNot.2: Informed people are kept up to date, with no say in or ownership of the work.

A.q: What is the main purpose of a cost breakdown structure?
options: To list who may approve any spending
To split costs into accounts by the WBS
To show when each payment will occur
To record the project's risks and costs
A.why: A CBS breaks the project costs into categories or accounts aligned to the WBS, for budgeting and cost control.

whyNot.0: Spending authority is a governance matter, not what a CBS shows.
whyNot.2: When payments fall is a cash-flow or schedule question; the CBS shows what costs belong where.
whyNot.3: Risks are recorded in the risk register, not the CBS.

B.q: What does an organisational breakdown structure (OBS) show?
options: The cost accounts and the budget
B.why: An OBS is the hierarchy of organisations, teams and people involved in the project, with their reporting lines.

whyNot.1: Products are shown in the product breakdown structure.
whyNot.2: Work packages are shown in the work breakdown structure.
whyNot.3: Cost accounts are shown in the cost breakdown structure.

B.q: In RACI, which role is kept up to date on progress but is not asked for input?
B.why: Informed is one-way communication: the person is told about progress or decisions but is not asked for input.

whyNot.1: The Accountable person owns the outcome and signs it off, so they are far more than informed.
whyNot.2: Consulted is two-way: the person's input is sought before or during the work.
whyNot.3: The Responsible person actually does the work.

B.q:
Which TWO of the following are good practice when completing a RACI chart?
1. Exactly one Accountable per work package
2. At least one Responsible per work package
3. Make everyone Accountable for something
4. Leave unclear work packages blank
B.why: One Accountable avoids confusion over who answers for the work, and at least one Responsible makes sure somebody actually does it.

whyNot.0: Making everyone Accountable for something is not a rule; it can spread accountability too thinly.
whyNot.1: Leaving packages blank creates gaps, which is exactly what a RAM exists to prevent.
whyNot.2: Neither forcing accountability on everyone nor leaving blanks is good practice.

C.q: Spending on an office move is over budget, but the project manager cannot tell which part of the work caused it. Which structure would most help?
C.why: A CBS allocates costs to accounts aligned to the WBS, so actual spend can be compared with budget for each part of the work.

whyNot.1: The OBS shows who is involved, not where the money is going.
whyNot.2: The PBS shows the products, not their costs.
whyNot.3: The stakeholder register records stakeholders, not costs.

C.q: A project manager wants to confirm that every work package has a named owner. Which tool shows this most directly?
C.why: The RAM maps every work package against the people involved, so a package with no owner stands out immediately.

whyNot.0: The OBS lists the people, but does not link them to individual work packages.
whyNot.1: The CBS links costs to the work, not people.
whyNot.3: The PBS lists products, not who owns the work.

C.q: For the work package 'Install network cabling', the IT lead does the work and the project manager signs it off. The facilities manager advises on building access beforehand. Which RACI letter should the facilities manager have?
C.why: The facilities manager gives input before the work: two-way communication, so they are Consulted.

whyNot.0: The IT lead is Responsible, as the person doing the work.
whyNot.1: The project manager is Accountable, as the person who signs it off.
whyNot.3: Informed people are only told about progress; the facilities manager is actively asked for advice.

reteach.title: Moving house
reteach.question: You and your partner are moving house with help from a removals firm and a friend with a van. How would you keep track of the money, the people and who is doing which job?

blocks.body: Split the moving budget into pots that match the jobs: packing materials, the removals firm, cleaning the old house. That is your CBS. Sketch who is involved: you, your partner, the removals firm, your friend. That is your OBS. Then draw a grid with the jobs down the side and the people across the top, and mark who does each job, who decides, who to ask and who to tell. That grid is your RAM, in RACI form.

blocks.text: Two people can share the doing (R), but only one person should answer for each job (A). Otherwise everyone assumes someone else has it covered.

explain.body: Project costs broken into categories or accounts aligned to the WBS. The project manager uses it to allocate budget to each piece of work, then to compare actual costs with that budget so overruns can be spotted and traced.

test.q: A cost breakdown structure is normally aligned to which other structure?
test.why: The CBS is aligned to the WBS so that every cost belongs to a defined piece of work.

whyNot.0: The OBS shows people; costs are organised around the work instead.
whyNot.2: The RAM assigns people to work; it is not the basis of the cost accounts.
whyNot.3: The risk register records risks; it is not a breakdown structure for costs.

explain.body: The hierarchy of the organisations, teams and people involved, showing reporting lines and authority. It can include suppliers and contractors. It shows WHO, not what they are doing.

test.q: Which of the following would appear as an item in an OBS?
test.why: An OBS shows the organisations, teams and people involved, so a team is the item that belongs there.

whyNot.0: Installing cabling is work, which belongs in the WBS.
whyNot.2: A cost account belongs in the CBS.
whyNot.3: Completed removals is work or a milestone, not part of the organisation.

explain.body: The WBS crossed with the OBS: a matrix of work packages against people or teams. It makes sure every work package has an owner, avoids gaps and duplicated effort, and shows who needs to be involved in each piece of work.

test.q: What is the main reason a project manager builds a RAM?
options: To show the costs of each team
To set the order of the work
To give each package an owner
test.why: A RAM assigns roles for each work package, so every package has a clear owner and nothing falls between the gaps.

whyNot.0: Costs are shown in the CBS, not the RAM.
whyNot.1: The order of the work is set in the schedule.
whyNot.3: Products are listed in the PBS.

explain.body: Responsible: does the work. Accountable: ultimately answerable and signs it off; only one per work package. Consulted: asked for input, two-way. Informed: kept up to date, one-way. One person can be both A and R.

test.q: What is the difference between Responsible and Accountable in a RACI chart?
options: R signs off; A does the work
R is asked; A is only told
They mean the same in RACI
R does it; A answers for it
test.why: The Responsible person does the work; the Accountable person is ultimately answerable for it and signs it off.

whyNot.0: This reverses the roles: R does the work and A signs it off.
whyNot.1: Being asked for input is Consulted and being told is Informed.
whyNot.2: They are deliberately different roles, though one person can hold both.
